key_insight: An operating system needs six interlocking components — vision, people, data, issues, process, traction — and weakness in any one undermines the rest
Traction discipline comes before vision work — teams that already run Rocks and L10 produce much more grounded vision documents than teams working from scratch
Structure the organization by function first — define all seats with 5 major roles before placing any names — then use GWC to fit people to seats
Half of companies have a visionary alongside their integrator — the dynamic is a partnership of complementary strengths, not a reporting hierarchy
A single grid evaluates each person against Core Values (plus/plus-minus/minus) AND GWC (yes/no) — with a recommended bar that sets the minimum acceptable score
Get it / Want it / Capacity to do it — all three must be yes for a person to be in the right seat, no exceptions
Rocks are 3-7 quarterly priorities per person, each specific/measurable/attainable with exactly one named owner — focus is the discipline, not activity
90-day cycles create natural urgency and a psychological buildup effect — pre-scheduling sessions causes preparation energy to accumulate that shorter or longer cycles do not generate
EOS runs on a three-tier rhythm — weekly L10 (90 min), quarterly planning (full day), annual planning (2 days off-site) — each with its own purpose and discipline
A 90-minute weekly leadership meeting with seven fixed agenda items and strict time allocations — the most important is IDS (60 minutes), but discipline at all 7 items is what makes the cadence work
Three-step issue resolution — Identify the root cause (not the stated symptom), Discuss once with everyone speaking once, Solve into a concrete to-do — keeps meetings productive
5-15 weekly activity-based leading indicators with one named owner per number, displayed on a 13-week rolling grid with the WHO column elevated to the leftmost position
A 2-page document answering 8 questions — the Vision page captures who the company is and where it's going, the Traction page captures how it gets there over the next year and quarter

Core values are discovered through a 4-step team exercise (clone → traits → narrow → debate), not invented through brainstorming — and they must be operationalizable for hire/fire/review/reward decisions
Two sub-parts — Purpose/Cause/Passion (the WHY beyond money) and Niche (the ONE thing the company does exceptionally well) — together they define the "sweet spot" the company stays inside
A single specific BHAG ten years out — one entry, not a list, with a number and a date that make success unambiguous
Four concrete sub-parts — Target Market, 3 Uniques, Proven Process, Guarantee — each sharp enough to drive real sales and marketing decisions, not abstract positioning fluff

A vivid, concrete snapshot of the business three years out — required fields are future date, revenue, profit, measurables, plus a bullet description vivid enough to pull the team forward and concrete enough to guide decisions

Every business runs on 5-15 core processes — the work is to identify them, agree on names, document them at the 20/80 level, assign owners from the Accountability Chart, and enforce consistent usage across the organization

Three stages — Identify the core processes as a leadership team, Document each at the 20/80 level in 2-10 pages of major steps with bullet sub-steps, then Compile into one package and train everyone who touches them

Every person in the organization has at least one weekly activity-based number that traces up through the Accountability Chart to a leadership Scorecard number, creating a cascade of real accountability from the top to the floor
